evidence: Ran the full suite (212 pass): test 'an async config is waited for' has a config delayed 25 ms; a config, a wrapper and an action declare the plain name Database, are created only after 'Database ready' and receive the finished object, not a promise. A hand-run app printed connect called, connect done, makeFind got { id: 7 }.

Test 'an async config needed by other configs, a wrapper and several actions is called once': one call and one finish recorded for Database, and two configs (one itself async), a wrapper and two actions all received the identical object.

Same test: container keys include Database and no Promise<Database>; getInstance() is the finished object and getMetadata().name is Database. The README example run prints 'Settings: @Config' for its async config.

Test 'an async config that fails stops startup': message is 'Database: function makeDatabase (<path>) failed while waiting for it: no connection', cause is the original TypeError, only Clock and Database were called, a second start calls the config again, and after the fault is lifted a file added in between is picked up. Seen by hand too with a rejecting config.
Scanner test and startup test: configs returning Database and Promise<Database> give the single line 'Database: returned by both makeDatabase (a.ts) and connectDatabase (a.ts)', nothing called.

Scanner tests and two startup tests (Wrapper, Action): 'makeLate (a.ts): is marked @Action but returns Promise<Late>; only a @Config may be asynchronous...' arrives in the one error with a not-exported and an unknown-dependency mistake, files that throw at module level were not imported, and no follow-up 'Late is not a known component' line appears.

CLAUDE.md 4.3 and 4.7 carry the rule in Indonesian; README has the section 'Asynchronous configs' saying startup sets no time limit and a config should set its own timeout, and its example config loadSettings is now async Promise<Settings>. test/readme.test.ts type-checks and starts that example with unchanged output, and asserts both documents.
package.json dependencies is still ts-morph only (file untouched); npm run typecheck, npm test (212 pass, 0 fail) and npm run build (dist with .js and .d.ts) all passed.
